purpose: How a managed Wi-Fi provider turns a signed venue offer into a working, segmented, documented network: surveying the site's RF and physical facts instead of assuming them, placing and channeling access points against measured coverage and busy-hour capacity targets, separating guest, point-of-sale and back-office traffic with enforceable SSID/VLAN boundaries, selecting cloud-manageable hardware the monthly service can actually operate, building a captive portal whose every collected field is disclosed and consented, executing cabling and installation within site and code constraints, and validating, documenting and gating the finished site into monitoring operations.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the provider is a small local or regional operator deploying designed business Wi-Fi for restaurants, motels, offices, retail and multi-tenant properties under a monthly management subscription; enterprise-campus and carrier deployments are out of frame

spectrum occupancy, wall construction, cabling pathways, power availability and code constraints are site-specific facts that only a survey establishes; nothing in this KB asserts them for any venue in advance

electrical-code, low-voltage-permit, plenum-cable and payment-card-segment obligations are named as obligation classes with a duty to verify current rules in the operating jurisdiction and with the venue's payment processor; no compliance state is asserted as achieved by default
hardware, licensing and installation costs appear only as mechanisms and trade-off shapes, never as specific figures asserted as fact
content is educational operating knowledge for the deployment practitioner, never personalized legal, financial or insurance advice for a specific venue
exclusions: productizing and pricing the Wi-Fi-as-a-service offer, venue-type value propositions, per-AP/per-site subscription architecture, positioning against one-time installers, and deal qualification — the managed Wi-Fi offer and target venues KB owns that territory

remote monitoring and alerting, ongoing firmware hygiene, SLA design and uptime reporting, support tiers and escalation, renewal and retention, and expansion to additional sites or adjacent services such as cameras and VoIP — the monitoring, management and SLA operations KB owns that territory; this KB ends at the gate that hands a validated site into those operations
interception, inspection-for-resale or sale of guest traffic or guest identity data in any form, and any captive-portal data collection that is not disclosed to the guest and agreed by the venue
stating invented equipment prices, license fees, labor rates or throughput guarantees as fact; costs and performance appear only as selection mechanisms and measured validation results
assuming spectrum congestion, wall materials, cable paths, PoE availability or permit requirements for any site before the survey establishes them

personalized legal, tax or insurance advice about a venue's compliance posture; obligation classes are named and deferred to current rules in the venue's jurisdiction and payment-processing agreements

competency_questions.question: What must the engineering scope capture from the signed offer before anyone drives to the site, and what does 'done' mean for this deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEPLOYMENT_SCOPE_INTAKE lists the coverage areas, device and operations-system inventory, ISP handoff, portal expectations and the acceptance definition the deployment will be judged against

competency_questions.question: Which site facts must be measured rather than assumed, and why does knowing the venue type never substitute for a survey?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_FACTS_NOT_ASSUMPTIONS names the fact classes (spectrum, construction, pathways, power, code) that only a survey establishes, and RF_SITE_SURVEY shows how each is captured

competency_questions.question: How does the survey convert a floor plan and measured spectrum into coverage and busy-hour capacity targets a design can be tested against?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RF_SITE_SURVEY yields measured attenuation and occupancy, and COVERAGE_CAPACITY_MODEL turns them into per-area client-count and throughput targets tied to the venue's busiest hour

competency_questions.question: How are access points placed, channeled and powered so the design meets its targets without dead zones or co-channel interference, and what happens when the RF-best spot is visually unacceptable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AP_PLACEMENT_PLAN gives the placement, channel-reuse and transmit-power logic plus the rule that aesthetic relocations re-verify against the coverage model

competency_questions.question: How are guest, point-of-sale and back-office traffic separated, and what proves the separation actually holds on the installed network?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SSID_VLAN_SEGMENTATION defines the segment matrix and its firewall policy, and VALIDATION_TESTING includes the cross-segment reachability tests that must pass before go-live

competency_questions.question: What may the provider never do with guest traffic and guest data, and how is that boundary built into the network rather than merely promised?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GUEST_ISOLATION_PRIVACY states the no-interception and no-sale rules with client isolation as the technical enforcement, and PORTAL_DISCLOSURE_CONSENT covers the collection side

competency_questions.question: What obligation class does a payment-card segment carry, and how does the deployment handle it honestly without asserting compliance it cannot certify?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POS_SEGMENT_COMPLIANCE names the payment-card-security obligation class, the isolation and change-control duties it implies, and the verify-with-processor-and-current-rules stance

competency_questions.question: How is the hardware platform chosen for a managed service, and how do licensing terms and cloud tenancy enter the choice as mechanisms rather than assumed prices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HARDWARE_PLATFORM_SELECTION makes remote manageability and segmentation support the disqualifying criteria with licensing as a per-deal mechanism to reconcile, and CLOUD_MGMT_ARCHITECTURE defines the tenancy and credential custody

competency_questions.question: How is the captive portal built so that every collected field is disclosed, consented and agreed with the venue before a single guest record is stored?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAPTIVE_PORTAL_DESIGN covers the splash flow and its collection choices and PORTAL_DISCLOSURE_CONSENT supplies the disclosure text, consent capture and venue sign-off requirements

competency_questions.question: How are cabling, PoE power and code constraints planned and installed without disrupting a venue that is open for business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CABLING_AND_POWER_PLAN gives the pathway, PoE-budget and code-obligation planning and INSTALLATION_EXECUTION gives the low-disruption, labeled-workmanship execution rules

competency_questions.question: How does the venue's existing internet service integrate with the new network, and which handoff facts must be verified with the ISP before install day?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ISP_HANDOFF_INTEGRATION names the demarcation, WAN-mode and addressing facts to verify and the double-NAT and modem-bridging pitfalls to clear in advance

competency_questions.question: What tests must pass before a site is declared live, and what happens to defects the tests uncover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VALIDATION_TESTING lists the coverage, throughput, roaming, isolation and portal tests with pass conditions, and PUNCH_LIST_REMEDIATION routes every failure through fix-and-retest rather than waiver-by-silence

competency_questions.question: What does the as-built documentation package contain, and why does the provider's own future service depend on it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOCUMENTATION_PACKAGE enumerates the as-built map, cable labels, segment matrix, config export, portal disclosure text and credential custody terms, and CONFIG_BASELINE_TEMPLATE explains the standardized baseline the docs snapshot

competency_questions.question: What must be true before the site passes from the deployment crew into monitoring operations, and what does the venue owner learn at handoff?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_HANDOFF_BRIEFING covers what the owner and staff are taught and asked not to change, and OPS_HANDOFF_GATE states the pass conditions — validation clean, docs delivered, monitoring enrolled and alerting verified — that end the deployment phase

glossary.definition: An on-site measurement pass that captures existing spectrum occupancy, neighbor networks and interference sources, wall and ceiling construction, and signal attenuation across the floor plan, producing the measured facts a Wi-Fi design is built from.
The radio unit that serves Wi-Fi clients in an area; in a managed deployment every AP is cloud-managed, PoE-powered, and placed by the design plan rather than wherever an outlet happens to be.
The broadcast network name a client joins; one physical network typically carries several SSIDs (guest, operations, point-of-sale) that map to different VLANs and firewall policies.

Splitting one physical network into isolated logical networks so guest devices, payment systems and back-office machines cannot reach each other except through explicitly allowed, documented firewall rules.

The splash page a guest sees before getting internet access, used for terms acceptance, optional disclosed data collection, and bandwidth or session policy; its data collection must be disclosed to the guest and agreed by the venue.
A wireless setting that prevents devices on the same guest SSID from seeing or reaching each other, protecting each guest from other guests and reinforcing that the guest segment is internet-only.

The total Power-over-Ethernet wattage a switch can deliver versus what the attached APs, cameras and phones draw; exceeding it causes devices to brown out or drop, so the plan reserves headroom before anything is energized.

Performance loss caused by nearby APs transmitting on the same channel and sharing airtime; the channel-reuse plan spaces same-channel APs apart and trims transmit power to keep their cells from overlapping.

The record of what was actually installed — AP locations on the floor plan, cable runs and labels, the SSID/VLAN matrix, config export and firmware version — as opposed to what was originally proposed.

Two devices performing network address translation in series, typically the ISP's modem-router in front of the provider's gateway; it breaks captive portals, remote management and port-dependent services until the upstream device is bridged or the topology is redesigned.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for wifi_design_deployment_and_handoff work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Translate the signed offer into an engineering scope before any survey or purchase: which indoor and outdoor areas must have coverage, what the venue runs on the network today (POS terminals, kitchen printers, door locks, cameras, music, office PCs), expected guest volume and its busiest hour, who the ISP is and where its service enters the building, what the portal is supposed to do, and the written definition of done the venue will sign against. The intake also reconciles what the offer promised with what the platform and site can deliver, surfacing gaps to the offer owner now instead of on install day.

excluded: pricing or re-negotiating the offer itself
the survey measurements the scope will later be checked against

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the venue or the offer owner changes the coverage areas, device inventory or acceptance definition

pros.claim: A written scope with an acceptance definition prevents the deployment from being judged against unstated expectations
pros.example: the motel owner who assumed the parking lot was covered finds it listed as excluded in the scope sheet he signed, not discovered at acceptance

cons.claim: Scope captured only from the owner's memory misses systems staff quietly depend on
cons.example: a restaurant scope that never mentioned the cordless kitchen printer that turns out to sit on the same network as the POS

failure_modes: starting the survey with no device inventory and discovering the POS vendor's requirements during install
leaving 'done' undefined so the venue withholds acceptance over items the offer never included
acceptance_tests: the scope sheet lists coverage areas with inclusions and exclusions, every network-dependent system the venue runs, the ISP handoff location, portal intent, and a signed definition of done
revisit_triggers: the venue adds areas, devices or systems after signing
the offer owner amends what was sold

nodes.definition: Hold the line that spectrum congestion, wall and ceiling construction, cable pathways, power and PoE availability, landlord rules and code constraints are facts a survey establishes for this specific site, never assumptions imported from venue type. Two restaurants of the same size differ in kitchen interference, wall materials and attic access; a design copied from the last similar job fails in ways the provider then eats under the management subscription. Every design-driving input is therefore tagged measured, verified-with-a-party (ISP, landlord, POS vendor), or unknown-and-blocking — and an unknown blocks the step that needs it.

included: the fact classes only a survey establishes
the rule that unknowns block dependent steps
excluded: design decisions made from the facts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a design built on a tagged assumption fails on site, or a fact class proves assumable safely across many jobs

pros.claim: Tagging every design input by how it was established exposes the guesses before they become installed mistakes
pros.example: the plan shows 'attic pathway: unknown-and-blocking' so nobody quotes a one-day install before the crawlspace is actually opened

cons.claim: Insisting on verification for every input adds visits and delay on small, simple sites
cons.example: a four-AP office deployment waiting a week for a landlord answer about a wall that a five-minute look could have settled

failure_modes: designing from the last similar venue and discovering concrete-block walls after the hardware order
assuming the ISP handoff mode and meeting double NAT on install day
acceptance_tests: every design-driving input in the plan carries a measured, verified, or unknown-and-blocking tag, and no dependent step proceeds on an unknown
revisit_triggers: a tagged fact is contradicted on site
renovation, tenancy or ISP changes invalidate previously verified facts

nodes.definition: Walk the site and measure what the design must survive: 2.4/5/6 GHz occupancy and neighbor networks captured per area, non-Wi-Fi interferers noted where the venue actually has them (kitchen microwaves, DECT handsets, refrigeration, cordless peripherals), signal attenuation through the actual walls and floors measured with a test AP or survey tool, and the physical layer recorded — ceiling types, mounting options, existing cable, riser and attic access, electrical and switch locations — all onto an annotated floor plan with photos. The survey is scheduled to catch the venue's real conditions: a restaurant surveyed at 10am misses the dinner-rush interference the design must handle.

included: spectrum and interference capture per area
physical and pathway documentation with photos

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-install measurements diverge from survey readings, or a survey tool or method upgrade changes what can be captured

pros.claim: Measured attenuation and occupancy turn placement from guesswork into arithmetic the validation can later be checked against
pros.example: measuring that the motel's block wall eats most of the through-wall signal justifies per-room-cluster APs before the owner balks at the count

cons.claim: A survey is a snapshot; conditions it did not witness stay invisible
cons.example: the Friday-night food truck generator and its point-of-sale hotspot parked next to the patio never appear in a Tuesday survey

failure_modes: surveying at a quiet hour and missing time-of-day interference the venue lives with daily
recording signal readings but not the ceiling and pathway facts the installers need
acceptance_tests: the survey report contains per-area spectrum captures, measured attenuation values for the walls that matter, an annotated floor plan with photos of pathways and mounting points, and a note of when and under what conditions it was taken
revisit_triggers: validation results contradict survey measurements
the venue renovates, re-arranges, or reports a new interference source

nodes.definition: Convert the survey into testable design targets, keeping coverage and capacity distinct: coverage says where a usable signal must exist (every guest room, the patio, the walk-in office), capacity says how much concurrent airtime each area needs at the venue's busiest hour — a motel lobby at check-in, a restaurant dining room on Friday night, a retail floor in December. Each area gets a target client count, a per-client experience expectation stated as an application class (browsing, streaming, card transactions), and a minimum signal level, so validation later has numbers to pass or fail rather than a vibe. Targets derive from the venue's stated volumes, not from invented throughput promises.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed busy-hour client counts after go-live diverge from the targets the design was built to

pros.claim: Separating capacity from coverage stops the classic failure of a bar that shows full signal and still cannot load a page at peak
pros.example: planning the sports-bar main room for its match-night crowd of simultaneous phones instead of for its floor area

cons.claim: Busy-hour estimates come from the owner's impressions and can be badly off in either direction
cons.example: a motel owner's guess that guests 'mostly just check email' colliding with a lobby full of streaming children

failure_modes: designing to floor area instead of concurrent clients and failing at peak occupancy
promising a specific throughput figure the provider cannot control end to end
acceptance_tests: every scoped area has a coverage threshold, a busy-hour client target and an application class, and no target is expressed as a guaranteed speed promise to the venue
revisit_triggers: the venue's occupancy pattern or use of the network changes materially
validation shows targets were set unrealistically high or low

nodes.definition: Turn targets into a placement map: AP locations chosen against measured attenuation and the mounting reality the survey recorded (hard-lid versus drop ceiling, no visible boxes in the dining room, corridor versus in-room trade-offs in a motel wing), a channel-reuse plan that keeps same-channel cells apart, transmit power trimmed so cells hand off cleanly instead of overlapping, and 2.4 GHz treated as the congested legacy band while 5/6 GHz carries the design. The plan states, per AP, why it is where it is — which target it serves — so that when a location is challenged on looks or access, the cost of moving it is knowable instead of argued.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a validation walk contradicts the predicted coverage, or the venue vetoes planned locations

pros.claim: A per-AP rationale makes aesthetic relocation negotiations concrete instead of positional
pros.example: showing the restaurant owner that moving the dining-room AP behind the beam sacrifices the patio target he asked for, and letting him choose

cons.claim: Dense placement for capacity raises hardware and license mechanism cost the offer may not have absorbed
cons.example: a motel wing that honestly needs per-room-cluster APs against a proposal sized for corridor coverage

failure_modes: placing APs where mounting is easy rather than where targets need them
running maximum transmit power everywhere and creating sticky-client and co-channel problems
acceptance_tests: each planned AP carries a location, mounting method, channel, power setting and the target area it serves, and predicted coverage meets every per-area threshold
revisit_triggers: validation finds a coverage hole or roaming failure
an AP location is vetoed for aesthetics, access or landlord rules

nodes.definition: Design the segment matrix that keeps the venue's money systems and its guests apart: separate SSIDs mapped to separate VLANs for guest, point-of-sale, back-office and (where present) IoT devices like cameras and door locks, with default-deny firewall policy between segments and each exception — a manager tablet that must reach the POS reporting port, a kitchen printer the ordering system calls — written down with its business reason. The guest segment is internet-only with client isolation on; the POS segment carries nothing but payment traffic; wired ports are assigned to VLANs deliberately so a guest cable in the lobby cannot land on the office network.

included: default-deny inter-segment policy with justified exceptions
excluded: the live reachability testing that proves isolation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an isolation failure, a new spanning device class, or a processor requirement changes the required segment shape

pros.claim: Default-deny with written exceptions makes the segment design auditable by whoever inherits the site
pros.example: the exception log shows exactly why the manager's tablet can reach one POS port, so a later technician does not 'clean up' a rule the ordering flow depends on

cons.claim: Strict segmentation breaks conveniences staff silently used on the old flat network
cons.example: the hostess can no longer AirPlay the lobby music from her phone because guest and ops are finally separate, and the change lands as a complaint

failure_modes: leaving any-to-any rules between segments because a device 'did not work' during setup
assigning wired ports to VLANs by whatever the previous installer left configured
acceptance_tests: the segment matrix maps every SSID and wired port to a VLAN, inter-segment policy is default-deny, and every exception carries a named device and business reason
revisit_triggers: the venue adds a device class that spans segments
an isolation test or audit finds an undocumented allowance

nodes.definition: Encode the guest-privacy boundary as network behavior, not policy prose: the provider does not intercept, inspect-for-resale, or sell guest traffic or identity data, full stop, and the guest segment is built so the temptation has no mechanism — client isolation on, no traffic-content logging beyond what operating the service requires, DNS and analytics features that would profile individual guests left off unless they are disclosed and venue-agreed, and guest data never joined to third-party marketing datasets by the provider. What the venue itself does with disclosed portal data is the venue's declared choice; the provider's job is that nothing is collected or observed beyond what the disclosure says.

included: no-interception and no-sale rules as configuration
excluded: the venue's own use of data it lawfully collects and discloses

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform feature change, a privacy-law change in the operating jurisdiction, or a monetization request tests the boundary

pros.claim: Building the boundary into configuration survives staff turnover and sales pressure in a way a policy document does not
pros.example: a marketing vendor's 'presence analytics' pitch dies at the fact that per-client tracking is disabled platform-wide, not at a meeting

cons.claim: Refusing guest-data monetization closes an ancillary revenue stream competitors may offer the venue
cons.example: losing a motel deal to a bidder whose free-hardware offer is funded by selling guest marketing profiles

failure_modes: enabling a platform analytics feature that profiles guests because it came on by default
retaining guest browsing logs 'just in case' beyond operational need
acceptance_tests: client isolation is on for the guest SSID, no per-guest profiling or content-inspection feature is enabled undisclosed, and log retention matches operational need
revisit_triggers: the platform adds or auto-enables analytics features
the venue or a partner requests guest-data uses beyond the current disclosure

nodes.definition: Treat the point-of-sale segment as carrying a payment-card-security obligation class the provider supports but never certifies: card-handling systems live on their own isolated segment, reachable from nowhere the design does not explicitly allow, with changes to that segment logged and the segment's shape documented for the venue's processor conversations. The provider's honest posture is fixed: it builds and evidences isolation, it names the obligation class, and it tells the venue to verify current requirements with its payment processor and current payment-card industry rules — it does not declare the venue 'compliant', which depends on far more than the network.

included: change logging and evidence for the venue's processor
excluded: certifying or asserting the venue's compliance status

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a POS vendor change, a processor requirement, or a payment-card rule revision alters what the segment must evidence

pros.claim: A documented, evidenced payment segment turns the processor's questionnaire from a panic into a lookup
pros.example: the cafe owner answers the acquirer's network questions from the segment matrix and isolation test results in the handoff package

cons.claim: The honest no-certification stance can lose against a competitor who casually promises 'PCI compliance included'
cons.example: a franchise operator picks the bidder who claimed the network alone makes them compliant, a claim nobody can honestly make

failure_modes: asserting the venue is compliant because the VLANs are separate
letting a convenience exception into the payment segment during troubleshooting and never removing it
acceptance_tests: the payment segment's isolation is evidenced by reachability test results, its allowed flows are documented, and all client-facing language names the obligation class and defers certification to the processor and current rules
revisit_triggers: the venue changes POS vendor or payment flow
payment-card industry network requirements are revised

nodes.definition: Choose the hardware platform as a service decision, not a box decision: the disqualifying tests are whether the gear can be centrally cloud-managed (because the monthly subscription is operationally impossible without remote visibility and control), whether it supports the segment matrix (multiple SSIDs mapped to VLANs with per-segment policy), whether the vendor's licensing mechanism — per-AP, per-site, subscription or perpetual — is reconciled against what the offer sold, and whether the line is one the provider can stock, spare and standardize on across its book. Consumer-grade gear fails the first test regardless of price; an exotic best-of-breed line fails the standardization test. The bill of materials prices out per deal from current vendor terms; no cost in this KB is a fact, only a mechanism to check.

included: manageability and segmentation-support as disqualifying tests

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vendor licensing, product line, or supply conditions change, or the fleet standard fails a design requirement

pros.claim: Standardizing on one cloud-managed line makes every later site cheaper to run than the hardware discount ever was
pros.example: one spare AP model in the van and one management console covering every client site, versus a museum of one-off routers inherited from cheapest-bid installs

cons.claim: Committing to one vendor exposes the whole book to that vendor's pricing and licensing changes
cons.example: a platform's shift to mandatory subscription licensing repricing every planned deployment in the pipeline at once

failure_modes: buying consumer gear that cannot be remotely managed and discovering the subscription cannot be serviced
ordering hardware before reconciling the vendor's per-AP license mechanism with what the offer included
acceptance_tests: the chosen platform passes the manageability and segmentation tests, its licensing mechanism is reconciled in writing against the offer, and the bill of materials is priced from current vendor terms for this deal
revisit_triggers: the vendor changes licensing, retires the line, or has a supply gap
a design requirement exceeds the standardized platform's capability

nodes.definition: Structure the cloud management layer so the provider can run many venues without any venue being able to hurt another: one provider organization with a sub-tenant or site container per client, role-based access where technicians get what their tier needs and nothing more, admin credentials held by the provider in a password vault with the custody terms written into the client agreement, the venue given read or guest-management access where the platform allows it, and API or webhook hooks left ready for the monitoring stack that takes over after handoff. Guest-profiling analytics stay off per the privacy boundary. The architecture also answers the exit question in advance: what the venue receives if the relationship ends, so custody never becomes hostage-taking.

included: role-based access and credential custody terms
excluded: the live monitoring and alerting operation itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a staffing change, a platform tenancy-model change, or an exit dispute exposes a custody gap

pros.claim: Per-client tenancy with role-based access contains both technician mistakes and client curiosity
pros.example: a junior tech troubleshooting the taqueria cannot touch the motel's portal, and the motel owner's read access shows his site only

cons.claim: Provider-held credentials concentrate risk and invite lock-in accusations if exit terms are vague
cons.example: a venue's new IT consultant painting the provider as holding the network hostage because the agreement never said what happens to admin access at exit

failure_modes: running every client in one flat organization where one bad change propagates everywhere
leaving default or shared admin credentials that survive technician departure
acceptance_tests: each client is a separate tenant or container, access is role-scoped, credential custody and exit terms are written into the agreement, and monitoring hooks are configured and dormant-ready
revisit_triggers: a technician joins or leaves
the platform changes its tenancy, role or API model

nodes.definition: Build the guest's front door: the splash page carrying the venue's branding, the access method chosen with the venue (open with terms acceptance, simple code, or a disclosed opt-in form), terms-of-use acceptance, session and bandwidth policy so one downloader cannot starve the dining room, and the redirect experience after connect. Every field the portal collects exists because the venue chose it and the disclosure covers it — the design default is the minimum: no collection beyond terms acceptance unless the venue explicitly wants a disclosed program. The portal is also an operational component: it must survive platform updates, render on the phones guests actually carry, and fail open or closed by deliberate choice rather than accident.

excluded: the disclosure and consent text itself
guest-network privacy enforcement at the traffic layer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: guest completion problems, a venue data-program change, or a platform portal update

pros.claim: A deliberate bandwidth and session policy protects the shared experience the venue is actually buying
pros.example: the motel's per-device cap keeps one long-stay guest's console downloads from burying every other room at 9pm

cons.claim: Every portal step costs guest goodwill, and venues feel that cost immediately
cons.example: the coffee shop that demanded an email-gated portal watching guests give up at the form and complain to the barista

failure_modes: collecting fields nobody asked for because the platform template had them
a portal that renders broken on common phones so guests conclude the Wi-Fi is down
acceptance_tests: the portal flow is tested on current common phone platforms, every collected field maps to a venue-chosen, disclosure-covered purpose, and session policy is configured and recorded
revisit_triggers: the venue changes its data program or branding
a platform update alters portal behavior

nodes.definition: Make the portal's data collection lawful-by-design and honest-by-text: a plain-language disclosure on the portal stating what is collected, why, who receives it (the venue, and never sale by the provider), and how a guest can decline; affirmative consent captured for any marketing use rather than buried in terms; the venue's written sign-off on the exact fields and uses before the portal goes live; and the disclosure text preserved in the handoff documentation as the record of what guests were told. Consent and privacy obligations for guest data vary by jurisdiction — the node names the obligation class and requires verifying current rules where the venue operates rather than asserting a compliance recipe.

included: venue written sign-off on fields and uses
excluded: drafting the venue's full privacy policy as legal advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a jurisdictional privacy-rule change, a venue data-program change, or a mismatch found between collected and disclosed fields

pros.claim: A signed field-and-use record protects the provider when the venue's marketing ambitions grow later
pros.example: when the motel's new manager asks where the email list 'feature' went, the sign-off shows the venue chose terms-only collection at launch

cons.claim: Prominent disclosure depresses opt-in volume compared to the quiet-collection portals some venues have seen elsewhere
cons.example: the restaurant owner disappointed that honest opt-in yields a fraction of what a buried-consent vendor promised

failure_modes: collecting a field the disclosure never mentioned
going live on a verbal 'sure, collect emails' with no written venue sign-off
acceptance_tests: the live portal's collected fields exactly match the disclosed fields, marketing use has affirmative consent, the venue's written sign-off predates go-live, and the disclosure text is archived in the handoff package
revisit_triggers: the venue requests new fields or new uses
privacy or consent rules change in the operating jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Plan the physical plant before anyone pulls cable: runs routed along the pathways the survey actually found (attic, riser, conduit, surface raceway where the landlord allows), cable category chosen for the platform's needs, plenum-rated cable where air-handling spaces demand it as a code obligation class, a PoE budget computed across every powered device on each switch — APs, phones, cameras — with headroom reserved, switch port map drafted with VLAN assignments, and the permit question answered per site: low-voltage work is permitted and licensed differently by jurisdiction, so the plan names the obligation class and verifies current local rules rather than assuming. Landlord and historic-building constraints are written approvals, not hallway conversations.

included: plenum and permit obligation classes named per site
excluded: the mounting and termination work itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a code or permit rule check returns a different answer, or the powered-device inventory changes

pros.claim: A PoE budget with reserved headroom prevents the silent brownouts that masquerade as Wi-Fi flakiness for months
pros.example: the retail site whose APs rebooted nightly until someone noticed the camera retrofit had eaten the switch's power margin — avoided entirely by the budget line that reserved it

cons.claim: Conservative pathway and code planning inflates the install bid on sites where shortcuts would probably have survived
cons.example: quoting conduit and plenum cable for a strip-mall ceiling a cheaper bidder staples non-rated cable through

failure_modes: pulling non-plenum cable through an air-handling ceiling and facing rip-out at inspection
sizing the switch to the AP count and leaving no PoE or port room for the cameras the venue adds next quarter
acceptance_tests: every run has a routed pathway and cable class, the PoE budget covers all powered devices with stated headroom, code and permit obligation classes are answered for this jurisdiction, and landlord approvals are in writing
revisit_triggers: device additions change the power or port budget
a pathway is found blocked or disallowed during install

nodes.definition: Execute the install as a guest of a working business: work scheduled around service hours (a restaurant's closed morning, a motel's low-occupancy block), dust and ceiling work contained, every cable labeled at both ends against the port map as it is terminated, APs mounted per the placement plan with deviations flagged rather than improvised, patch panels dressed so the closet can be understood by a stranger, old equipment removed or clearly decommissioned rather than left humming, and each day ending with the venue operational — the POS working every night even mid-project. Workmanship is a service-economics decision: the provider will live with this plant for the life of the subscription, so every unlabeled cable is a future truck roll it sold itself.

excluded: design changes decided on the ladder

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: deviation flags accumulate on a job, or post-install support incidents trace back to workmanship shortcuts

pros.claim: Label-as-you-terminate and dressed closets convert every future support incident from archaeology into a lookup
pros.example: the tech who fixes the dead office drop in ten minutes because the label says which patch port and switch port it lands on

cons.claim: Working only around service hours stretches calendar time and multiplies site visits
cons.example: a restaurant install that takes four closed-morning sessions instead of one loud day the kitchen would not tolerate

failure_modes: leaving the POS dead overnight mid-project because cutover ran long
relocating an AP on the ladder for convenience without flagging it against the plan
acceptance_tests: all cables labeled both ends per the port map, mounted AP locations match the plan or carry a flagged deviation, the venue operated normally every service period during the install, and removed gear is out or marked decommissioned
revisit_triggers: a deviation flag changes coverage or the port map
the venue reports service disruption attributable to install work

nodes.definition: Integrate cleanly with the internet service the venue already buys: identify the demarcation point and who owns each box beyond it, verify with the ISP — before install day — whether its device can be bridged or must route (the double-NAT question that breaks portals and remote management), confirm addressing facts (static or dynamic, any PPPoE credentials the venue must recover), configure the provider's gateway as the network's single routing brain, and document the dividing line: the provider manages from its gateway inward, the ISP owns the circuit outward, and the venue knows whom to call for which failure. Where the offer includes failover, the secondary path is installed and actually tested by pulling the primary, not assumed from the box's spec sheet.

excluded: selling or reselling the internet circuit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an ISP change, equipment swap, or a portal/remote-management failure traced to the WAN handoff

pros.claim: A documented demarcation line kills the vendor-blame spiral that otherwise consumes support relationships
pros.example: when the circuit drops, the motel calls the ISP with the circuit ID from the handoff sheet instead of opening a Wi-Fi ticket and waiting out two vendors pointing at each other

cons.claim: The provider depends on ISP cooperation it cannot compel, and some handoffs stay ugly
cons.example: an ISP whose combo unit cannot be truly bridged, forcing a documented double-NAT workaround the portal has to be tested against

failure_modes: discovering on install day that the ISP router cannot be bridged
leaving the old ISP box routing so two devices fight over the network's brain
acceptance_tests: the WAN mode is verified with the ISP in advance, the gateway is the sole router or the exception is documented and tested, addressing facts are recorded, and the demarcation sheet names who owns what
revisit_triggers: the venue changes ISP or plan
the ISP swaps its equipment or changes the handoff mode

nodes.definition: Apply a standardized configuration baseline instead of hand-crafting each site: naming conventions for sites, APs and SSIDs that make fleet dashboards legible; the segment matrix realized as templated VLAN, firewall and wireless profiles; radio settings from the placement plan; management-plane hygiene (unique admin credentials from the vault, unused ports disabled, management traffic on its own VLAN); firmware pinned to a known-good version for install so validation tests a fixed target, with ongoing firmware lifecycle explicitly left to the operations KB; and a config export captured the moment validation passes — the baseline snapshot that documentation preserves and monitoring will treat as truth. Site-specific deviations from template live in a deviations list, not in tribal memory.

included: install-time firmware pinning and config export
excluded: ongoing firmware update cadence and patching

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurring deviations, platform setting deprecations, or incident patterns that trace to template choices

pros.claim: A templated baseline makes the tenth site cost a fraction of the first and makes every site legible to every technician
pros.example: any tech opening any client dashboard knows what an SSID named by convention is for, and a misnamed one is itself a finding

cons.claim: Templates fit the median site and quietly misfit the odd one unless deviations are disciplined
cons.example: the template's radio profile assuming drop ceilings underperforming in the one client site with open steel trusses

failure_modes: hand-configuring each site so no two are alike and every incident starts from zero
validating against whatever firmware shipped in the box and chasing behavior that changes mid-test
acceptance_tests: the applied config matches the template with every deviation listed, admin credentials are unique and vaulted, firmware matches the pinned version, and a config export is archived at validation pass
revisit_triggers: a deviation recurs across sites and belongs in the template
the platform deprecates settings the template uses

nodes.definition: Prove the deployment against its own targets before anyone calls it done: a coverage walk measuring signal in every scoped area against the model's thresholds, throughput sampling under realistic conditions, roaming tests walking active sessions across AP boundaries, the isolation matrix — from a guest device, attempt to reach POS, back-office and management addresses and record every result, in both directions — the portal flow on real phones including its disclosure text, wired ports checked against their VLAN assignments, and failover exercised by pulling the primary where sold. Timing matters: capacity claims are validated under load or at the venue's busy hour, not in an empty room at 10am. Every result lands on a pass/fail checklist with numbers, not impressions; failures go to the punch list, and the site cannot be declared live around them.

included: coverage, throughput and roaming tests against stated targets
portal and disclosure flow on real devices

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a field failure class escapes the suite, or targets change and the checklist must follow

pros.claim: A numeric pass/fail record converts acceptance from opinion into evidence both sides can sign
pros.example: the motel owner signs acceptance against a checklist showing every room class met its threshold, instead of walking around with his phone frowning

cons.claim: Honest validation, especially busy-hour testing, costs schedule and crew time that install-and-wave competitors do not spend
cons.example: holding the crew for a Friday-evening capacity test on a site that 'felt fine' on Wednesday afternoon

failure_modes: testing coverage in an empty venue and never testing capacity under load
running the isolation test in one direction only and missing a return-path hole
acceptance_tests: every scoped area passes its coverage threshold, the isolation matrix shows zero unexpected reachability in either direction, the portal flow and disclosure render on tested devices, wired ports match their VLAN map, and any sold failover was exercised by pulling the primary
revisit_triggers: any punch-list fix touches tested behavior
the venue reports a failure class the suite did not cover

nodes.definition: Run every validation failure through a visible loop instead of a shrug: each defect logged with its failed test, severity and owner; isolation failures treated as go-live blockers while cosmetic items can ride with a date; fixes made under the same discipline as the original work (deviations flagged, baseline updated, labels maintained); and the failed test re-run after the fix — plus any test the fix could plausibly have disturbed, since a channel change to fix one dead corner can degrade the room next door. The punch list is shared with the venue, which builds more trust than hiding it: an owner who watches three items get found, fixed and retested believes the checklist in a way no glossy handoff binder achieves.

included: defect logging with failed test and severity
retest of the fix and its blast radius
excluded: re-opening design decisions validation did not fail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurring defect classes point at a design or template cause rather than one-off installation slips

pros.claim: Retesting the fix's blast radius catches the second-order breakage that quick fixes cause
pros.example: the power bump that cured the patio dead spot gets caught re-creating co-channel interference in the dining room because the adjacent-area tests re-ran

cons.claim: A formal loop on every defect feels heavy on small sites with two trivial findings
cons.example: logging, classifying and retesting a mislabeled patch cable on a four-AP office where the fix took ninety seconds

failure_modes: fixing defects informally so nobody knows what changed after validation
declaring items fixed without re-running the failed test
acceptance_tests: every open defect carries a failed test, severity and owner; every closed defect shows a passing retest; and no isolation-class defect is open at go-live
revisit_triggers: a closed defect recurs
a fix invalidates previously passing tests

nodes.definition: Assemble the as-built record that the provider's own future service lives on: the floor plan with actual AP locations (deviations included), the cable map matching the physical labels, the switch port and VLAN map, the segment matrix with its exception log, the validation checklist with results, the config export and pinned firmware version, the portal disclosure text as shipped, the ISP demarcation sheet with circuit identifiers, photos of closets and pathways, and the credential-custody statement saying what the provider holds and under what exit terms. The package serves three readers: the provider's own technicians a year from now, the venue owner who wants proof of what was bought, and the successor provider whose existence the docs must tolerate — a package only its author can use is a lock-in instrument, not documentation.

included: as-built floor plan and cable map
validation results, config export and firmware version
portal disclosure text and demarcation sheet
excluded: operational runbooks owned by the monitoring operation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a doc-site mismatch is found, or the package format proves unusable by a reader it must serve

pros.claim: As-builts written from the actual install make every later support call cheaper for the life of the subscription
pros.example: diagnosing a dead conference-room drop from the port map over the phone instead of rolling a truck to trace unlabeled cable

cons.claim: A successor-usable package weakens the switching-cost moat some providers quietly rely on
cons.example: the venue's board using the excellent as-builts to solicit competing management bids at renewal

failure_modes: writing docs from memory weeks later so they describe the plan, not the site
omitting the exception log so the next technician deletes a rule the ordering flow needs
acceptance_tests: the package contains as-built plan, cable and port maps, segment matrix with exceptions, validation results, config export, firmware version, disclosure text, demarcation sheet and custody statement, and a spot-check confirms labels on site match the docs
revisit_triggers: any post-handoff change alters what the docs describe
a support incident reveals a doc-versus-site mismatch

nodes.definition: Teach the venue what it now owns and where the boundaries are: a walkthrough with the owner showing what was built against the scope sheet; the staff-level essentials — which network staff devices join, where the guest code or portal lives, what the do-not-change list contains (do not plug personal routers into wall ports, do not share the ops password with vendors, do not 'fix' the closet); how to reach support and what counts as an emergency; what the venue can self-serve (guest password rotation where offered) versus what goes through the provider; and the credential and exit terms stated aloud, not just buried in the package. The briefing is where segmentation survives contact with real staff behavior — a rule nobody explained is a rule that gets worked around by Friday.

included: owner walkthrough against the scope sheet
custody and exit terms said aloud
excluded: training the venue to administer the network

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: support incidents trace to staff actions the briefing was meant to prevent

pros.claim: Ten minutes of staff briefing prevents the personal-router and shared-password incidents that undo segmentation
pros.example: the front-desk clerk who now calls support instead of plugging her home router into the lobby port 'because the Wi-Fi felt slow'

cons.claim: Briefings decay with staff turnover and the provider rarely hears about the new hires
cons.example: six months later the new night manager has never heard the do-not-change list and improvises

failure_modes: handing a binder to the owner and briefing no one who actually touches the network
leaving self-serve boundaries vague so staff either call for everything or touch what they should not
acceptance_tests: the owner has walked the build against the scope sheet, on-shift staff heard the do-not-change list and support path, and the self-serve boundary is stated in the package the venue keeps
revisit_triggers: staff turnover at the venue
repeat support incidents caused by staff actions the briefing should prevent

nodes.definition: Hold the gate between building and operating: the site passes into the monitoring and SLA operation only when validation is clean or every open item is a dated, venue-acknowledged ride-along; the documentation package is delivered and spot-checked; the client briefing has happened; monitoring enrollment is not merely configured but proven — a test alert has actually fired and reached the operations queue; the config export and firmware version are archived as the baseline monitoring will compare against; and the venue has signed acceptance against the definition of done from the scope intake. A site that skips this gate becomes an operations mystery: alerts nobody mapped, documents nobody delivered, and a first outage diagnosed from scratch at the venue's worst moment.

included: pass conditions across validation, docs, briefing and acceptance
proven monitoring enrollment with a fired test alert
signed acceptance against the scope's definition of done
excluded: the monitoring thresholds and SLA mechanics themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operations intake contract changes, or post-gate incident patterns show a missing pass condition

pros.claim: A proven-alert requirement catches the silently unmonitored site before the first real outage does
pros.example: the test alert that never arrives exposes a webhook typo on handoff day instead of during the motel's Saturday-night outage

cons.claim: A hard gate delays revenue recognition and collides with everyone's urge to call the project finished
cons.example: the crew's next job waiting while a missing landlord approval document holds an otherwise perfect site at the gate

failure_modes: declaring the site live with monitoring configured but never proven end to end
letting acceptance ride on goodwill instead of the signed definition of done
acceptance_tests: validation is clean or all open items are dated and venue-acknowledged, the docs package is delivered and spot-checked, a test alert fired and reached the operations queue, the baseline export is archived, and acceptance is signed against the scope's definition of done
revisit_triggers: the operations intake contract changes what the gate must prove
a gated site produces early incidents that a gate condition should have caught

edges.why_related: the survey walks the areas and systems the scope sheet names, at the conditions the scope's busy hour implies
the survey exists to convert assumption-class inputs into measured or verified facts; anything it leaves unknown stays tagged blocking
coverage and capacity targets are set from measured attenuation, occupancy and the venue's observed conditions
each AP is placed to serve a stated per-area target; without targets, placement reverts to guesswork
placement may only use mounting, pathway and attenuation inputs that carry a measured or verified tag
the segment matrix is designed around the device and operations-system inventory the intake captured
the guest-privacy boundary is enforced on the guest segment the matrix defines
the payment segment's obligation-class handling builds on the isolation the matrix designs
AP class, radio capability and switch sizing follow from the capacity targets the model sets
a platform that cannot realize the segment matrix — multiple SSIDs to VLANs with per-segment policy — is disqualified regardless of price
tenancy, roles and credential custody are structured within whatever the chosen platform's cloud offers
the portal may only collect what the privacy boundary and disclosure allow; minimum collection is the design default
the disclosure text, consent capture and venue sign-off are written against the portal's actual fields and flow
cable runs, PoE budget and switch ports are planned to feed the APs where the placement plan puts them
pathways, plenum requirements and permit obligations enter the cable plan only as surveyed or verified facts
the crew installs against the routed runs, port map and PoE budget the plan fixed
the intake identifies the ISP, circuit and demarcation whose handoff mode must be verified before install day
the baseline's naming, roles and credential hygiene are instances of the tenancy architecture's rules
validation measures the installed plant; untested cable and unmounted APs cannot pass a coverage walk
validation tests the pinned firmware and templated config so results describe a fixed, reproducible target
portal, throughput and failover tests run across the WAN handoff and fail meaninglessly if it is unresolved
failures flow from the checklist into the logged fix-and-retest loop in order, never into informal fixes
the as-built package preserves the validated state — results, config export, firmware — not the intended one
the briefing walks the owner through the package the venue keeps; briefing without docs leaves nothing behind
the gate requires the punch list clean or every open item dated and venue-acknowledged
delivered, spot-checked documentation is a hard pass condition of the gate
a briefed owner and staff is a gate condition; an unbriefed venue generates the incidents operations then eats
mounting reality and venue aesthetics push installers to relocate APs from their RF-chosen positions on the ladder
edges.resolution_rule: the coverage target wins: any relocation is flagged as a deviation and re-verified against the coverage model before acceptance; if the venue insists on a location that breaks a target, the trade-off is shown and the venue's choice is recorded in the scope sheet

edges.why_related: the portal's marketing potential pulls toward collecting more guest data than the privacy boundary and disclosure permit
edges.resolution_rule: the privacy boundary wins unconditionally: only fields named in the disclosure and signed off by the venue are collected, undisclosed collection is removed on discovery, and no guest data is sold or joined to third-party marketing sets by the provider

edges.why_related: go-live pressure — an opening night, a booked event, revenue recognition — pushes to declare the site done before the suite completes
edges.resolution_rule: the validation suite wins for anything touching money systems or isolation: a venue-demanded early opening may run the guest SSID in a declared provisional state with ops segments held back, the punch list logged, and the gate passed only when the full suite is clean

edges.why_related: measured attenuation and channel occupancy directly cause the placement, channel and power choices the plan makes
a pinned, exported, templated baseline is what makes the gate's monitoring-enrollment and archived-snapshot conditions provable
a failed coverage, roaming or capacity test sends the placement and channel plan back for revision in the affected areas
every fix re-enters the suite — the failed test plus its blast radius — until the checklist is clean
both encode the same guest-data ethic at different layers: one forbids undisclosed observation of traffic, the other forbids undisclosed collection at the portal
the isolation matrix must include payment-segment reachability attempts in both directions, and a failure there is a go-live blocker
platform analytics that profile individual guests stay disabled in the tenancy configuration unless disclosed and venue-agreed
the shipped disclosure text and the venue's signed field-and-use record must be preserved in the handoff package

conflict_axes.name: rf_optimal_vs_venue_aesthetics
conflict_axes.description: The RF-best AP position is often the visually worst — center ceiling of a styled dining room, above the lobby art — and the venue pushes placement toward beams, corners and closets that eat the signal.
poles: place for the venue's look and mounting convenience
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: negotiate from the per-AP rationale: show what each candidate location costs against the targets, let the venue choose with the trade-off visible, and record the choice; never silently accept a target-breaking spot

conflict_axes.name: coverage_everywhere_vs_capacity_where_it_counts
conflict_axes.description: Spreading a fixed AP count thin covers every corner weakly, while concentrating airtime at the busy zones leaves edges dark; the same hardware cannot maximize both.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the per-area targets arbitrate: capacity targets rule the zones that earn the venue money, coverage thresholds rule the rest, and any area that cannot get both becomes an explicit scope conversation

conflict_axes.name: guest_convenience_vs_data_minimization
conflict_axes.description: The smoothest guest experience is zero-step open access, while venue marketing wants forms and profiles; both pull against the minimum-collection, full-disclosure default.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to minimum collection; any venue data program must be disclosed on the portal, affirmatively consented for marketing use, and signed off in writing — friction is the honest price of collection

conflict_axes.name: segmentation_rigor_vs_staff_usability
conflict_axes.description: Default-deny segmentation breaks the casual cross-network habits staff built on the old flat network — casting to the lobby TV, printing from a phone — and each accommodation erodes the boundary.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grant exceptions only as named-device, written-reason rules in the exception log; if the venue needs a workflow, engineer a documented path for it rather than widening a segment

conflict_axes.name: hardware_cost_vs_manageability
conflict_axes.description: Consumer and unmanaged gear wins every up-front price comparison and loses the subscription: without central cloud management the monthly service cannot be delivered at any margin.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: manageability and segmentation support are disqualifying tests, not weighted factors; cost competition happens only among platforms that pass, via the per-deal bill of materials

conflict_axes.name: install_speed_vs_workmanship
conflict_axes.description: Every labeled cable, dressed closet and contained-dust session costs install hours a lump-sum bid wants back, but the provider services this plant for the life of the subscription.
poles: plant the provider can afford to service for years
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: price workmanship as service economics: the label and the dressed closet are bought once and repay on every future incident; shortcuts are sold only as explicit, documented venue choices

conflict_axes.name: go_live_pressure_vs_validation_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Opening nights, booked events and the crew's next job all push to declare the site live before coverage, capacity and isolation are proven.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: isolation and money-system tests never yield; guest-only provisional operation with ops segments held back is the only early-open compromise, and it is declared, logged and time-boxed

conflict_axes.name: survey_depth_vs_deal_economics
conflict_axes.description: An exhaustive multi-visit survey is overkill for a four-AP office and barely enough for a three-building motel; survey effort must scale without ever dropping to zero.
poles: keep pre-sale and pre-install cost proportionate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale survey depth to site complexity and stakes, but the fact classes never go unverified — a small site gets a short survey, not an assumed one

conflict_axes.name: documentation_thoroughness_vs_handoff_speed
conflict_axes.description: The complete as-built package competes with the pressure to close the project, invoice, and move the crew; docs written later describe memories, not sites.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write docs during install and validation, not after; the gate's delivered-and-spot-checked condition makes backfilling structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged

conflict_axes.name: platform_lock_in_vs_client_portability
conflict_axes.description: Provider-held tenancy and credentials are operationally necessary during the term but shade into hostage-taking if the venue cannot leave with a usable network and records.
poles: venue's ability to exit with its network
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep admin custody during the term but write the exit terms into the agreement and build the docs package a successor could use; retention should be earned by service, not by withheld passwords

edge_cases.description: A motel wing built of concrete block eats through-wall signal, so corridor APs that look fine on the plan leave in-room dead zones
edge_cases.trigger: the survey measures high-attenuation construction between corridor and rooms
edge_cases.mitigation: measure per-wall attenuation during the survey, plan in-room or door-adjacent placement per room cluster, and validate room classes individually rather than sampling the corridor

edge_cases.description: The ISP's combo modem-router cannot be bridged, and the resulting double NAT breaks the captive portal and remote management
edge_cases.trigger: the WAN handoff mode was assumed instead of verified with the ISP before install day
edge_cases.mitigation: verify bridge capability with the ISP during scope intake; where bridging is truly impossible, design and document the workaround and test portal and management through it explicitly

edge_cases.description: During the isolation test a guest device successfully reaches a POS terminal
edge_cases.trigger: a VLAN misassignment or a leftover any-to-any firewall rule survives into validation
edge_cases.mitigation: treat as the highest-severity blocker: freeze go-live, fix the rule or assignment, re-run the full bidirectional isolation matrix, and record the failure and fix in the handoff evidence

edge_cases.description: The venue owner asks the crew to quietly collect guest emails without putting it on the portal disclosure
edge_cases.trigger: a marketing idea arrives after the disclosure was signed off
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse undisclosed collection categorically; offer a disclosed opt-in version with updated venue sign-off, and note that consent obligations vary by jurisdiction and must be verified before launch

edge_cases.description: A historic-building landlord bars drilling and visible conduit through the dining room's original plaster
edge_cases.trigger: property rules surface after placement assumed normal pathways
edge_cases.mitigation: capture landlord and heritage constraints as written approvals during the survey, and redesign runs around approved pathways — existing chases, surface raceway where permitted — before any hardware order

edge_cases.description: A multi-tenant retail strip's neighbors saturate 2.4 GHz, drowning any design that leans on the legacy band
edge_cases.trigger: the survey's spectrum capture shows dense neighbor occupancy
edge_cases.mitigation: design 5/6 GHz-first, keep 2.4 GHz to the minimum SSIDs that genuinely need it, and plan channels around the measured occupancy rather than the theoretical map

edge_cases.description: The switch's PoE budget is silently exceeded when the venue's camera retrofit lands on the same switch mid-project
edge_cases.trigger: powered devices are added after the budget was computed
edge_cases.mitigation: reserve headroom in the original budget, and make any added powered device recompute the budget before it is energized; symptoms like random AP reboots trigger a budget re-check first

edge_cases.description: The restaurant's Wi-Fi degrades only during dinner rush, when the kitchen microwave, DECT handsets and a packed dining room combine
edge_cases.trigger: a daytime survey and an empty-room validation both missed the venue's real operating conditions
edge_cases.mitigation: observe or simulate the busy hour in the survey, validate capacity under load or at the busy hour, and leave channel-plan margin for the interferers the kitchen actually contains

edge_cases.description: Weeks after handoff, staff plug a personal router into a lobby wall port to 'fix slow Wi-Fi', bridging segments
edge_cases.trigger: an open wall port plus an unbriefed staff member
edge_cases.mitigation: disable unused ports and pin port-to-VLAN assignments in the baseline, put the no-personal-equipment rule in the staff briefing and the do-not-change list, and let monitoring flag rogue devices

edge_cases.description: Validation passes in an empty venue at mid-morning and the network still collapses at full Friday occupancy
edge_cases.trigger: capacity was never tested under load, only coverage
edge_cases.mitigation: test capacity with load generation or schedule a busy-hour validation pass before final acceptance, and treat an empty-room pass as provisional for capacity targets

edge_cases.description: The chosen platform requires a per-AP cloud license the proposal never accounted for, surfacing after the hardware order
edge_cases.trigger: licensing terms were assumed from a previous deal instead of reconciled for this one
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile the vendor's current licensing mechanism against the offer in writing before purchase, and route any gap to the offer owner as a scope conversation rather than absorbing it silently

edge_cases.description: The venue demands live guest Wi-Fi for a booked event before segmentation and validation are complete
edge_cases.trigger: an immovable venue date collides with an unfinished deployment
edge_cases.mitigation: offer the declared provisional state only: guest SSID up with client isolation and internet-only policy, ops and payment segments held down, the arrangement time-boxed and logged, and the full gate passed before ops traffic flows

workflow.action: Translate the signed offer into an engineering scope
workflow.description: Capture coverage areas, the device and systems inventory, ISP and demarcation, portal intent, and the written definition of done
workflow.gate: coverage inclusions and exclusions, every network-dependent system, the ISP handoff and the acceptance definition are recorded and signed

workflow.action: Survey the site's RF and physical facts
workflow.description: Measure spectrum, interference and attenuation, and document pathways, mounting, power and constraints with photos
workflow.artifact: survey report with annotated floor plan
workflow.gate: every design-driving input carries a measured, verified or unknown-and-blocking tag, and no blocking unknown is carried forward

workflow.action: Set coverage and busy-hour capacity targets
workflow.description: Convert survey data and venue volumes into per-area thresholds, client counts and application classes
workflow.gate: each scoped area has a coverage threshold and a busy-hour capacity target, with no guaranteed-speed promises

workflow.action: Draft the AP placement, channel and power plan
workflow.description: Place each AP against targets and mounting reality, with a channel-reuse and power plan and a per-AP rationale
workflow.artifact: placement map with channel and power plan
workflow.gate: predicted coverage meets every per-area threshold and each AP carries its rationale and mounting method

workflow.action: Design the SSID/VLAN segment matrix and privacy boundaries
workflow.description: Map SSIDs and wired ports to VLANs with default-deny policy, justified exceptions, guest isolation and the payment segment's obligation-class handling
workflow.gate: guest is internet-only with client isolation, the payment segment is isolated, and every exception carries a named device and business reason

workflow.action: Select the hardware platform and structure the cloud tenancy
workflow.description: Apply the manageability and segmentation disqualifiers, reconcile licensing against the offer, and set up per-client tenancy with credential custody
workflow.artifact: bill of materials and tenancy design
workflow.gate: the platform passes both disqualifying tests, licensing is reconciled in writing, and tenancy, roles and custody terms are defined

workflow.action: Build the captive portal and its disclosure
workflow.description: Construct the splash flow, session policy and any venue-chosen collection, with disclosure text and written venue sign-off
workflow.artifact: portal configuration with signed disclosure record
workflow.gate: collected fields exactly match the disclosed fields, marketing use has affirmative consent, and the venue signed off before go-live

workflow.action: Plan cabling and power, then execute the installation
workflow.description: Route runs and budget PoE per the plan, then install around service hours with label-as-you-terminate discipline and flagged deviations
workflow.artifact: labeled installed plant with cable map and deviation flags
workflow.gate: runs match the plan or carry flags, the PoE budget holds with headroom, code obligation classes are answered for this jurisdiction, and the venue operated through every service period

workflow.action: Integrate the ISP handoff and apply the config baseline
workflow.description: Resolve the WAN mode verified with the ISP, make the gateway the single router, and apply the templated baseline with pinned firmware
workflow.artifact: applied baseline with WAN integration record
workflow.gate: the gateway is online as sole router or the exception is documented, remote management is reachable, and firmware matches the pin

workflow.action: Validate the deployment end to end
workflow.description: Run the coverage walk, throughput and roaming tests, the bidirectional isolation matrix, portal flow, port checks and any sold failover, under realistic load
workflow.artifact: completed validation checklist with numeric results
workflow.gate: every test passes or its failure is on the punch list; no isolation-class failure is open

workflow.action: Fix and retest every punch-list defect
workflow.description: Log each defect with its failed test and severity, fix under change discipline, and re-run the failed test plus its blast radius
workflow.artifact: closed punch list with retest evidence
workflow.gate: all blockers closed with passing retests; remaining ride-alongs are dated and venue-acknowledged

workflow.action: Assemble documentation, brief the client, and pass the operations gate
workflow.description: Deliver the spot-checked as-built package, brief owner and staff, prove monitoring with a fired test alert, archive the baseline, and obtain signed acceptance
workflow.artifact: delivered handoff package with signed acceptance
workflow.gate: docs delivered and spot-checked, briefing held, a test alert reached the operations queue, the baseline export is archived, and acceptance is signed against the definition of done

priority_rationale: The frame nodes — scope intake and the facts-not-assumptions rule — come first because every later decision is only as good as what was captured and measured; the survey feeds the coverage and capacity model, which drives placement, while the segment matrix and its privacy and payment boundaries are designed in parallel from the intake because hardware selection must satisfy both the RF and the segmentation requirements; platform, portal, cabling and ISP work converge on installation and the templated baseline; validation then proves the whole build against its own targets, remediation closes what validation finds, and documentation, briefing and the operations gate come last because they compose a proven site into an artifact the monitoring operation can inherit without archaeology.

dominance_rules.rule: Surveyed site facts dominate venue-type assumptions in every design decision
dominance_rules.rationale: two venues of the same type differ in exactly the facts that break designs — construction, spectrum, pathways, power
dominance_rules.trigger: a design input is about to be filled from experience with similar venues instead of from this site's survey
dominance_rules.action: tag the input unknown-and-blocking and measure or verify it before the dependent step proceeds

dominance_rules.rule: Guest privacy and disclosure dominate every marketing and monetization appetite
dominance_rules.rationale: undisclosed collection or traffic exploitation breaches the business's foundational boundary and poisons the venue relationship it feeds on
dominance_rules.trigger: anyone — venue, partner, or platform default — proposes collecting or observing guest data beyond the current disclosure
dominance_rules.action: block the collection until it is disclosed on the portal, affirmatively consented where marketing use is involved, and signed off by the venue; sale of guest data is refused outright

dominance_rules.rule: Segment isolation dominates convenience for every network under management
dominance_rules.rationale: one any-to-any shortcut quietly dissolves the boundary that protects the venue's money systems
dominance_rules.trigger: a device 'does not work' and the fast fix is widening inter-segment policy
dominance_rules.action: engineer a named-device, written-reason exception or a proper path; a failed isolation test is a go-live blocker without appeal

dominance_rules.rule: RF targets dominate aesthetics, within trade-offs the venue chooses with open eyes
dominance_rules.rationale: a beautiful network that fails its coverage targets becomes the provider's support burden under the subscription
dominance_rules.trigger: an AP location is challenged for looks, access or landlord preference
dominance_rules.action: present the measured cost of the alternative location against the targets; record whichever trade-off the venue then chooses in the scope sheet

dominance_rules.rule: The validation gate dominates schedule and go-live pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an unproven network fails at the venue's busiest, most expensive moment, and the subscription's first impression never recovers
dominance_rules.trigger: an opening date, event or invoicing milestone pushes to skip or truncate the suite
dominance_rules.action: hold the gate; offer only the declared guest-only provisional state with ops segments down and the arrangement time-boxed

dominance_rules.rationale: the monthly service is operationally impossible on gear the provider cannot see and control remotely
dominance_rules.trigger: a cheaper unmanaged or consumer-grade option appears during platform selection or a venue offers its existing gear
dominance_rules.action: disqualify it regardless of price; compete on cost only among platforms that pass the manageability and segmentation tests

dominance_rules.rule: Obligation-class honesty dominates compliance shortcuts and compliance theater
dominance_rules.rationale: payment-card, permit, plenum and consent obligations vary by jurisdiction and processor, and false certainty transfers liability to the provider
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal, conversation or document is about to assert a compliance state as achieved
dominance_rules.action: name the obligation class, evidence what the network actually does, and defer certification to the venue's processor and current rules in its jurisdiction

dominance_rules.rule: The documented baseline dominates ad-hoc field tweaks
dominance_rules.rationale: monitoring and every future technician reason from the baseline; an undocumented tweak makes the site illegible
dominance_rules.trigger: a field change is made during install, remediation or troubleshooting
dominance_rules.action: land the change in the baseline and deviations list and refresh the config export, or revert it

dominance_rules.rule: The venue's exit rights dominate lock-in convenience at handoff
dominance_rules.rationale: retention earned by withheld credentials and unusable docs is hostage-taking, and it detonates reputationally in small markets
dominance_rules.trigger: documentation or credential-custody choices would leave the venue unable to change providers with a working network
dominance_rules.action: keep custody during the term but write exit terms into the agreement and build the docs package a successor could operate from
